chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Al-As and Hammad, from Hariz, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams), upon them be peace, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you.'
And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you.

He said: 'That which you intend to manumit him for. Do not say: I will manumit him for five thousand and leave a thousand for him, but rather look to that which you intended for him and give it to him from it.'

key_terms.أَضْمَرْتَ: You intended or resolved in your heart
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: How should a master fulfill the Quranic command to give a mukatab slave from the wealth of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the interpretation of 'from the wealth of Allah' in Surah An-Nur, specifying that the master must pay the slave the full agreed-upon manumission price without deducting a portion for the master's own benefit. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integrity of the mukatabah contract, ensuring the slave receives the complete financial commitment intended for their freedom.
